affected_systems: Mucous membranes of nose and throat; skin infections
symptoms: Fever, sore throat, swollen glands, difficulty breathing and swallowing, thick grey membrane in the throat
transmission: Spread through respiratory droplets (coughing, sneezing), direct contact or contamination
complications: Can lead to myocarditis (heart damage), kidney damage, nerve damage and even death
vaccination: DTaP and Tdap Vaccination; Tdap vaccination for every 10 years (Booster dose)
prevalence_and_course: Very rare and spreads fast; Resolves within days to weeks

affected_systems: Often affects lungs; also affects heart, kidney, spine, and brain
symptoms: Prolonged cough, chest pain, weight loss, fever and night sweats (Active TB); asymptomatic (Latent TB)
transmission: Spread through coughing, sneezing, and saliva (kissing or sharing food)
at_risk_groups: Weakened immune systems (HIV/AIDS), diabetes, malnutrition, alcohol or tobacco users
complications: Can lead to serious health complications and be fatal if untreated
treatment: Treatable with combination of antibiotics (DOTS protocol: Rifampicin, Isoniazid, Pyrazinamide, Ethambutol)
prevalence_and_course: Common and spreads fast; Takes 6 months or more to treat

symptoms: Profuse watery diarrhea ('rice-water stools'), vomiting, rapid dehydration, muscle cramps, thirst
transmission: Contaminated drinking water and food via the fecal-oral route
at_risk_groups: Populations in flood zones, refugee camps, and areas lacking potable water and sanitation
complications: Hypovolemic shock, acute kidney injury, severe acidosis, death within hours if untreated
vaccination: Oral Cholera Vaccines (OCV: Shanchol, Euvichol, Dukoral)
treatment: Immediate Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS), intravenous fluids, and antibiotics (doxycycline, azithromycin)
prevalence_and_course: Endemic and epidemic in vulnerable areas; acute illness resolving in days with timely rehydration

affected_systems: Respiratory tract, skin, and lymphatic system; impacts central nervous system
symptoms: High fever, cough, coryza, conjunctivitis, Koplik spots inside the mouth, and maculopapular rash spreading downward
transmission: Airborne transmission via respiratory droplets, sneezing, coughing, and aerosol persistence
at_risk_groups: Unvaccinated young children, malnourished infants (Vitamin A deficiency), pregnant women
complications: Severe pneumonia, encephalitis, corneal blindness, subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE)
vaccination: MMR (Measles, Mumps, Rubella) / MR vaccine administered in two doses
treatment: Supportive care, hydration, antipyretics, and therapeutic high-dose Vitamin A supplementation
prevalence_and_course: Highly contagious; rash and acute febrile symptoms typically resolve in 10 to 14 days

affected_systems: Central nervous system (peripheral nerves, spinal cord, and brain parenchyma)
symptoms: Paresthesia and tingling at the bite site, fluctuating fever, progressing to hydrophobia, aerophobia, aggressive hallucinations, paralysis, and coma
transmission: Saliva inoculated through bites, scratches, or mucous membrane contact with infected mammals (primarily dogs and bats)
at_risk_groups: Veterinarians, dog handlers, forest workers, and populations in canine rabies-endemic countries
complications: Progressive fatal viral encephalomyelitis; case fatality rate approaches 100% once clinical symptoms appear
vaccination: Pre-exposure cell-culture prophylaxis; post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) vaccine series accompanied by Rabies Immunoglobulin (RIG)
treatment: Strictly post-exposure prophylaxis prior to symptom onset; strictly palliative once clinical signs manifest
prevalence_and_course: Incubation period ranges from weeks to months; clinical disease is lethal within 7 to 10 days
